title: A leper and a centurion (Matthew 8:1–13)
hookLine: an outcast and an occupier are the first healed after the sermon
carry: many shall come from east and west
tomorrow: what if the call to follow comes on a funeral day?

cards: Group photo, and everyone drifts toward the middle, where the light is best. Matthew starts at the edges. "When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him."
The Sermon on the Mount is behind him now. And the first two people Matthew shows reaching him: a man with leprosy, whom the law kept living apart, and a centurion, an officer of a foreign army.

teach.b: The leper kneels: "Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean." Watch the order: "Jesus put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou clean." The touch comes first.
Then Jesus sends him to the priest with the gift Moses commanded, back into the life of his people.

In Capernaum the centurion asks help for a servant lying sick at home, and won't even let Jesus come: "Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed."

teach.h: NOT SO GREAT FAITH IN ISRAEL.
teach.b: Jesus marvels: "I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel."

teach.h: A TABLE FOR EAST AND WEST.
teach.b: Then he widens the table: "many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven."

teach.h: MANY SHALL COME FROM EAST AND WEST.
teach.b: Look back over the week and the same thread runs through it: strangers from the east at the start, Galilee of the nations by the sea, and now an officer from outside Israel.
An outcast and an outsider, healed first, and a table with room at both ends of the sky.

how: In the Catholic Mass, just before communion, the people say words drawn from the centurion's: Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; some other liturgies echo the line too.

o: two fishermen called beside the sea
an outcast and an outsider, healed first
two enemies who made peace in Rome

s: Jesus healed the leper first, and only then touched him
Jesus put forth his hand and touched him, saying, I will; be thou clean. the touch comes first.
Jesus sent the healed man to show himself to the priest
and to offer the gift that Moses commanded.
the centurion begged Jesus to come under his roof
he said he wasn't worthy, and asked Jesus to speak the word only.

games.q: at your church potluck, a family new to town, from another country and another faith, stands by the door unsure where to sit. what fits Matthew 8?
o: walk over and offer them seats at your table.
point them toward the welcome desk and go back.
wait to see if someone they know shows up.
games.why: Jesus said many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob. the table has room.

practice: Count on your fingers the people at the edges of your week: the coworker who eats alone, the neighbor nobody visits, the new family down the street.
Stop at each finger long enough to see a face, and let the last one be the person you'll sit beside next.

wordCard.voice: A leper and a centurion. The first two healed after the sermon: a man kept apart, and an officer from outside Israel.

orig.note: Greek: centurion, an officer over soldiers. Matthew's word in 8:5.

carryVoice: Your line: many shall come from east and west. A week of Matthew, and the table keeps widening. Week done.
